newsitem.title: GERMANY: Premiere to launch German digital TV pilot project.
newsitem.headline: Premiere to launch German digital TV pilot project.

text.p: German pay television broadcaster Premiere said on Friday it planned a digital TV pilot project in which 30,000 of its customers would take part, but the project's content and start date have yet to be set.
A Premiere spokesman confirmed that "Premiere Digital" would offer sport, an electronic TV guide and pay-per-view showings of feature films, sports events and concerts.

The pilot project is an answer to Germany's only existing digital venture, the Kirch group's DF1 product launched last year, which has fallen far short of sales targets and had just 20,000 subscribers by November.

Premiere, which has won viewers for its pay TV with its offering of live German soccer, is pressing ahead with digital TV in its bid to outmaneouvre DF1 -- even though it is part owned by DF1 owner, Bavarian media mogul Leo Kirch.
Kirch owns 25 percent of Premiere, while publisher Bertelsmann and France's Canal Plus both own 37.5 percent.
Digital television operates by using a set-top decoder to unscramble encoded broadcast signals, while offering the possibility to charge subscribers on a per-view basis.
